content: A Rice Krispie treat is a dessert or snack that is prepared using Rice Krispies cereal, melted margarine or butter, and melted marshmallows. Occasionally, seasonal marshmallows or cereals are incorporated to create holiday-themed variations of the treat. While these snacks are often made at home, they are also commercially available in many stores, typically sold under the Rice Krispies brand. There are numerous variations of the traditional Rice Krispie treat. For example, caramel can be used as a substitute for marshmallows, or condensed milk can be added to the mixture before incorporating the Rice Krispies. Other variations include using corn syrup and peanut butter, adding mandarin oranges, or flavoring with vanilla. A notable alternative involves replacing marshmallows with chocolate, resulting in a treat known as Chocolate Crackles. Kellogg's has also introduced commercial versions of both the marshmallow-based and chocolate-based treats, marketed under the name Rice Krispies Squares. Rice Krispie treats were invented in 1928 by Mildred Day, who was working for the Kellogg Company at the time. She developed the snack as a fundraising initiative for a Camp Fire Girls group. Mildred Day passed away in June 1996 at the age of 92. Kellogg's later created a cereal inspired by the Rice Krispie treat, which may have been the first cereal derived from a dessert that was itself based on a cereal. This product, known as Kellogg's Rice Krispies Treats cereal, experienced a brief surge in popularity and received a 6 out of 7 rating on the breakfast review website Mr. Breakfast. However, this cereal has become increasingly difficult to find in recent years. A page on the Kellogg's website provides assistance in locating some of their rarer cereal products.
